what: The -Seed parameter of scripts/run-game.ps1 (Issue #349's addendum, scope point 4), prokinut into the engine as --seed and applied to the loaded fixture document as PrototypeCommandLog.Seed before the world is constructed (Main.Session.cs, LoadFixture). This closes the gap the gate-decisions log recorded on 2026-08-02: run-game.ps1 had -Fixture but no way to reach a seed other than the one the fixture document bakes in.

base.howObtained: git log -1 --format=%H, run at the repository root before this checkpoint's changes

howTheOverrideReachesTheWorld: Main.cs reads --seed with the same CommandLineArguments.Read helper every other optional flag uses, parses it as UInt64, and passes it to LoadFixture. LoadFixture applies it with '_fixtureLog = _fixtureLog with { Seed = seed }' before constructing PrototypeWorld — the identical record-with pattern DungeonFortress.Simulation.Tests already uses (e.g. PrototypeReturningRaiderTests.cs, RouteSeed = 20_260_729UL) to run a fixture at a seed other than its own. No line in DungeonFortress.Simulation moves: PrototypeCommandLog.Seed already accepted any ulong the document schema allows.

criterion5_twoSidedCheck.claim: Two runs of the same fixture with DIFFERENT -Seed values produce different canonical checksums and different screenshot bytes; two runs with the SAME -Seed value (or the fixture's own default) produce byte-identical output. A parameter that is accepted and silently ignored would pass only the second half.

runs.label: B: -Seed 20260726 (fixture's own baked-in seed, named explicitly) — divergence half of criterion 5
Default: no -Seed at all (backward compatibility — must equal B, since baseline.commands.v2.json's own seed is 20260726)

reading.sameSeedIsByteIdentical: A and A2 (both -Seed 20260729): checksum and screenshot SHA-256 match exactly — f4b23b00... both times, 56c2b2fd... both times.
reading.differentSeedDiverges: A (20260729) and B (20260726) differ in both checksum (f4b23b00... vs 54985f1c...) and screenshot SHA-256 (56c2b2fd... vs 10a9ee76...). The parameter is not being silently ignored.
reading.omittedSeedIsUnchangedBehaviour: Default (no -Seed) and B (-Seed 20260726, the fixture's own value, named explicitly) match byte-for-byte in both checksum and screenshot. Omitting -Seed keeps exactly the behaviour run-game.ps1 had before this parameter existed.
reading.conclusion: Both halves of criterion 5 hold: same seed -> identical output; different seed -> different output; and the parameter's absence is provably a no-op rather than an assumption.
